'''Nicanor Robles Austriaco Jr.''' [[Order of Preachers|OP]] is a [[Filipino Americans|Filipino-American]] [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] and [[Priesthood in the Catholic Church|Catholic priest]]. He is a professor of biology and professor of theology at [[Providence College]], in Providence, Rhode Island,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nicanor Austriaco O.P.|url=https://biology.providence.edu/faculty-members/nicanor-austriaco-o-p/|access-date=2021-01-05|website=The Department of Biology at Providence College|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-01-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113180602/https://biology.providence.edu/faculty-members/nicanor-austriaco-o-p/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a research fellow at the Center for Theology, Religious Studies, and Ethics, at the [[University of Santo Tomas]] in the Philippines.

== Early life and education ==
Nicanor Robles Austriaco Jr. was born on November 1, 1968, in the Philippines. He attended the [[University of Pennsylvania]] where he earned a Bachelor of Science Engineering (B.S.E.), ''summa cum laude'', in 1989. He went on to earn a PhD in biology from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)]] in 1996, where he was a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] pre-doctoral fellow in the laboratory of Professor [[Leonard Guarente]]. His doctoral research involved the characterization of the first aging genes in the budding yeast, ''[[Saccharomyces cerevisiae]]''.

In 1997, after a brief fellowship at the [[Ludwig Institute|Ludwig Institute of Cancer Research at the University College London]], he entered the Order of Friars Preachers. He attended the [[Pontifical Faculty of the Immaculate Conception]] at the [[Dominican House of Studies|Dominican House of Studies in Washington, D.C.]], where he earned his Master of Divinity degree and Licentiate in Sacred Theology. He completed his Doctorate in Sacred Theology at the [[University of Fribourg]] in 2015. Austriaco earned an M.B.A. degree from [[Providence College]] in 2020.

==Career==

Since 2005, Austriaco has served on the faculty of [[Providence College]]. In the same year, he became an investigator at the Rhode Island Idea Network of Biomedical Research Excellence (RI-INBRE) Program. A [[theistic evolution|theistic evolutionist]], Austriaco is staunchly critical of [[intelligent design]] (ID).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Farrell |first1=John |title=Intelligent Design: Losing the Catholics |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/intelligent-design-losing_b_790527 |access-date=17 September 2026 |work=[[HuffPost]] |date=5 December 2010}}</ref> He is also the founding director of {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20150504000430/http://www.thomisticevolution.org/ ThomisticEvolution.org]}}, which seeks to promote a Catholic approach to understanding evolution in the light of faith.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home|url=https://www.thomisticevolution.org/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150504000430/http://www.thomisticevolution.org/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=May 4, 2015|access-date=2021-01-05|website=Thomistic Evolution|language=en-US}}</ref> He is co-author of a book on Thomistic evolution.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thomistic Evolution|url=https://clunymedia.com/products/thomistic-evolution|access-date=2021-01-05|website=ClunyMedia|language=en}}</ref>

In 2011, Austriaco published a book titled ''Biomedicine and Beatitude: an Introduction to Catholic Bioethics''.<ref>{{Cite book|isbn=978-0813218823|title=Biomedicine and Beatitude: An Introduction to Catholic Bioethics|last1=Austriaco|first1=Nicanor Pier Giorgio|date=5 December 2011}}</ref> The book responds to questions raised in scientific and medical ethics from the perspective of the Catholic moral tradition that is grounded in a natural law and virtue ethic.

Austriaco has also spoken on numerous questions at the interface between science and religion. Most recently, he has proposed that the historicity of Adam and Eve can still be reconciled with the very best genomic science.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fr. Nicanor Austriaco, O.P. - Defending Adam After Darwin (FranU Bioethics Lecture Series) - YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1SSK5EaX6Xo|access-date=2021-01-05|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

Austriaco is currently a visiting professor of Biological Sciences at the [[University of Santo Tomas]] in the Philippines. As a fellow of the OCTA Research Team, he has been interviewed by Filipino TV channels on different aspects of COVID-19.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OCTA: COVID-19 cases sa NCR patuloy ang pagtaas|url=https://cnnphilippines.com/videos/2020/12/22/OCTA--COVID-19-cases-sa-NCR-patuloy-ang-pagtaas.html|access-date=2021-01-05|website=cnn|language=en}}{{dead link|date=February 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

== Research ==

In addition to his other work and publications, Austriaco is the founder and principal investigator of the Austriaco Lab. The laboratory is located at [[Providence College]] and is primarily an undergraduate research laboratory that investigates [[cell death]] using the budding yeast, ''[[Saccharomyces cerevisiae]]'', as a model organism.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lin|first1=Su-Ju|last2=Austriaco|first2=Nicanor|date=2014-02-01|title=Aging and cell death in the other yeasts, Schizosaccharomyces pombe and Candida albicans|url= |journal=FEMS Yeast Research|language=en|volume=14|issue=1|pages=119–135|doi=10.1111/1567-1364.12113|pmid=24205865|pmc=4000287|issn=1567-1356|doi-access=free}}</ref> Because of the pandemic, the lab has pivoted to developing a yeast based delivery platform for a [[COVID-19]] vaccine that can be easily deployed in developing countries.<ref>{{Cite web|website=[[The Varsitarian]]|title='Like Yakult': UST researcher eyes yeast to deliver oral Covid-19 vaccine|url=https://varsitarian.net/sci-tech/20201207/like-yakult-ust-researcher-eyes-yeast-to-deliver-oral-covid-19-vaccine|access-date=2021-01-05|language=en-US}}</ref>
